newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat volume swells on hedging as prices fall.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat volume swells on hedging as prices fall.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures came to life on Tuesday with 87 contracts changing hands in a generally weaker market.
Trading was swollen by hedging between the January and March contracts, with some hedging also between January and May. These were the only contracts to trade.
January fell by A$4.00 a tonne to A$167.00 on 52 lots, March fell A$3.50 to A$170.00 on 21 lots and May fell A$4.50 to A$172.00 on 14 lots.
Settlement prices were mostly down by about A$4.50 a tonne, although nearby July 1997 contract rose by A$2.00 and distant September 1998 added A$5.50.
"It has been a big day," Chris Gray of C, A & L Bell Commodities Corp said. "A lot of the volume has gone through on the basis of those spreads."
Gray described the present market as "tricky" in its volatility. He had expected rising prices on weather effects.
"But you don't jump in front of a moving train and it really is on the way down." Gray believes the market will bottom soon, then rally on the next disruption to crop prospects.
